name: Versant Media Group, Inc.

profile.description: Versant Media Group is an independent media company spun off from Comcast's NBCUniversal and founded January 2, 2026, owning cable networks including USA Network and CNBC alongside digital platforms such as Fandango, Rotten Tomatoes, GolfNow, and GolfPass. Q2 2026 revenue was $1.644B (-3.8% YoY) as linear distribution fell 6.3% on subscriber losses, while adjusted EBITDA of $624M (~38% margin) and $350M of quarterly free cash flow fund a $0.375 quarterly dividend and accelerated buybacks. CEO Mark Lazarus, former chairman of NBCUniversal Media Group, is steering the company away from roughly 80% cable dependence toward digital and sports businesses. Market cap approximately $4.4B.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on the Growth sleeve (10 weight units; the 5yr revenue CAGR is excluded because standalone history is too short and Yahoo only provides FY2022-FY2025, leaving 8 units) [4]. D/E of 38.9% scores 1.0, forward P/E of 4.85 scores 1.0, and Yahoo Finance's PEG of 0.64 scores 1.0 at 2x weight [4]. ROE of 8.1% scores 0.54 at 2x weight, YoY revenue growth of -3.7% scores 0.54, and profit margin of 11.5% scores 0.57 [4]. Weighted result 7.74/10 rounds to 8. The dividend started in 2026, so the stock is classified Growth despite its 4.8% yield. Liquidity passes: 1.75M avg volume x $31.42 = ~$54.9M/day.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): In its first year Versant divested SportsEngine, acquired Full Swing, signed a five-year Bundesliga deal, and launched an ad-supported Fandango streaming service — meaningful extensions, but none yet a significant new revenue stream, as platforms grew only 0.8% in Q2 including the divestiture [1]. AI Deployment (1/2): Rotten Tomatoes is recruiting a VP to lead its AI strategy, indicating AI exploration without disclosed products or savings [2]. Market Share (1/2): CNBC posted its highest-rated day in over five years during the SpaceX IPO and Fandango is a leading movie-ticketing platform, but the cable networks are losing subscribers [1]. Pipeline (1/2): The Bundesliga package (300+ matches per year, 30+ on USA Network) and CNBC direct-to-consumer initiatives are named, though without revenue targets [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No R&D is disclosed.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (1/4): Versant articulates a strategy — use cable cash flow to build diversified digital businesses — rather than a purpose; CEO Lazarus's own framing is that the brands showed 'strength, durability and scale' [1][2]. Community Impact (0/2): No Versant foundation or community program was found for the newly independent company [6]. Employee Retention (0/2): The company is less than a year old with no tenure or turnover data, and it is still assembling its leadership team [3]. Insider Buying (2/2): FMP records seven open-market director purchases in March 2026, led by David Novak's 143,000 shares at $36.85 (~$5.27M), plus Gerald Hassell (~$361K) and Leonard Potter (13,500 shares, ~$510K) [5].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): Live news (CNBC), live sports (Golf Channel, Bundesliga on USA Network), and transactional platforms (Fandango ticketing, GolfNow tee times) are relatively defensible, but the core linear TV business is already in secular decline, and AI-generated video, AI search answers, and AI recommendation engines threaten audience time and digital referral traffic for content and review properties such as Rotten Tomatoes [1][2]. The company is exposed but not directly substituted. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-related revenue is disclosed; Rotten Tomatoes is only beginning to staff an AI strategy role [2].

infinite_game.summary: Versant is too young to judge fully, but its posture is mixed-to-finite. The explicit strategy — harvest cable cash flow while building digital and sports businesses — is a rational managed decline paired with diversification, and leadership is returning large amounts of capital through dividends and ASRs [1][2]. There is no Just Cause beyond strategy, and a $35M CEO pay package in year one signals a finite incentive structure [3].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The company's stated direction is to reduce reliance on pay-TV and build new businesses — a strategy, not an idealistic future state; the cause language centers on brand 'strength, durability and scale' [1][2].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership comes from long NBCUniversal careers, giving continuity, and the company has been hiring a new leadership bench in marketing and editorial; no evidence of a low-trust culture surfaced, but there is no evidence of exceptional trust either [2][3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary framing competitors as benchmarks for self-improvement was found; the focus is on defending distribution economics and audience share [1].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Versant is openly trying to move from a roughly 80% cable-reliant model toward diversified digital and sports businesses — a deliberate pivot, though still early and incremental [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management is investing in new platforms (Fandango streaming, Full Swing, Bundesliga rights) and divested SportsEngine to focus, accepting that the new businesses will take time to offset linear declines [1]. Heavy buybacks and dividends show a balance with near-term shareholder returns.

investment_thesis: Versant is a cash machine priced for liquidation. Q2 2026 adjusted EBITDA was $624M on $1.644B of revenue (~38% margin), six-month free cash flow reached $908M, and management raised full-year guidance to $6.2-6.45B revenue and $1.9-2.05B adjusted EBITDA while holding $1.0-1.2B of free cash flow [1]. At $31.42 the stock trades at 4.85x forward earnings with a 4.8% dividend yield and a Yahoo Finance PEG of 0.64, and the company is shrinking its share count through back-to-back $100M accelerated repurchases with ~$800M of authorization remaining [1][4]. Platforms revenue grew 9.3% excluding the divested SportsEngine, led by Fandango and GolfNow, and directors bought roughly $6M of stock in March 2026, led by David Novak's $5.27M purchase [1][5].
thesis_continued: The bear case is secular decline. Linear distribution — $954M, or 58% of Q2 revenue — fell 6.3% on subscriber losses, total revenue fell 3.8%, adjusted EBITDA fell 8.9%, and diluted EPS dropped to $1.49 from $2.09 [1]. Yahoo Finance shows earnings down 28.7% YoY, and the business was built around cable TV, 'an industry in obvious decline,' leaving management racing to build new businesses with cash flow from a shrinking core [2][4]. Net debt is about $1.5B ($2.95B debt vs. $1.48B cash), Lazarus is eligible for a $35M first-year pay package, and the shares have fallen from ~$41 in August to $31, near the bottom of a $27-59 52-week range [1][3][4].
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results and delivery of raised 2026 guidance ($6.2-6.45B revenue, $1.9-2.05B adjusted EBITDA, $1.0-1.2B free cash flow) [1]
Continued capital returns: a second $100M ASR in Q3 2026, ~$800M remaining authorization, and a $1.50 annualized dividend at a 4.8% yield [1][4]
Digital and sports expansion — Fandango's ad-supported streaming launch, the Full Swing golf acquisition, GolfPass growth, and a five-year Bundesliga rights deal with 300+ matches per year [1]
key_risks: Accelerating cord-cutting: linear distribution revenue fell 6.3% in Q2 2026 and is 58% of revenue, so any acceleration in subscriber losses overwhelms platform growth [1]
Advertising and affiliate renewal risk as a standalone cable network group without Comcast's scale in negotiations with distributors [2]
Capital-allocation and governance risk: acquisitions to diversify away from cable, plus a $35M first-year CEO pay package, could erode the cash returns that underpin the valuation [1][3]
